translations.answer: The original poster confirms the issue. The value max_angular_velocity=100 is specified in degrees per second (deg/s), not radians per second (rad/s). This value is too low for testing, and the flywheel will reach this upper limit when the motor is removed. Therefore, the diagnostic order should first clarify the unit and scale of max_angular_velocity, and then evaluate friction, damping, or motor model. The original poster does not provide the corrected specific value or curve, so this card only retains the unit conclusion.
translations.applicability: This applies to Isaac Sim 4.5.0-rc.36 / Isaac Lab commit RigidBodyPropertiesCfg; other versions should check the local schema/documentation.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author clipped the DCMotor output to non-negative values and cleared friction and damping. They then verified the unit and passed the remaining issue to the maintenance team.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The unit and scale of max_angular_velocity should be verified before checking the DCMotor's velocity_limit/velocity_limit_sim.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: The unit mismatch causing the drop and the force-induced overlimit should be recorded separately.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The unit issue was clarified and max_angular_velocity was set to deg/s, with the physical upper limit converted and configured accordingly.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab commit 09590912792d4421c84f053c5c13c31391bb5c30; Isaac Sim 4.5.0-rc.36; Windows 11 Pro 23H2; RTX 4060 Laptop; CUDA Toolkit 11.8.
translations.details.limits.0: The original poster did not provide the corrected specific value or retest curve.
translations.details.limits.1: The issue cannot be closed simply because the force-induced overlimit was not resolved.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author acknowledged the incorrect value as a configuration error; the maintenance team did not respond to the remaining force-induced overlimit, and the issue was later closed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the flywheel appear to decelerate when there is no friction during force application?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why does the angular velocity exceed max_angular_velocity when a force is applied, but comply with it after the force is removed?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Misinterpreting simulation limit as rad/s could result in an execution constraint difference of about 57.3 times the real machine limit; units should be standardized and independent limit testing should be performed before deployment.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed max_angular_velocity=100 is in degrees per second (deg/s) and the flywheel was found to be too low in testing.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The internal cause of the force-induced overlimit is not determined in the original thread.
translations.details.symptoms.0: All explicit friction and damping are set to 0, DCMotor torque is clipped to non-negative, but the flywheel speed decreases during torque reduction.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The angular velocity exceeds max_angular_velocity when a force is applied, but complies with it during sliding.
translations.media_summaries.0: The original poster's curve is explained in the text: torque decreases after about 100 ms, speed coincides, and speed stabilizes at ~170 ms after torque is zero. This card does not include pixel-level data from images, and the unit conclusion is based on the author's subsequent text verification.
translations.source.title: Isaac Sim's max_angular_velocity unit inconsistency with common radians per second, and force-induced overlimit still unexplained
translations.title: What is the unit trap in max_angular_velocity when the frictionless flywheel in Isaac Sim shows unexpected deceleration?
